projects.title: Action-Conditioned Robot World Model
projects.alt: Ground truth, official baseline and our generated robot videos for three manipulation tasks
projects.summary: Predicting future video from an image and a robot action sequence, with action-conditioned adaptation and inverse-dynamics consistency.
projects.result: Top Excellence Award, graduate track (2nd place)
sections: Problem
Generate 16 future frames from one observation and a sequence of five joint target positions plus a gripper value. The generated motion needs to follow the requested action as well as look plausible.
Approach

Led the project from task analysis to final submission. Adapted Cosmos-Predict2.5 with LoRA and an action embedder, used two-stage training, and introduced an inverse-dynamics consistency objective to connect the generated motion to the action input.
Evaluation
The final Private score was 0.19226 (lower is better), earning 2nd place in the graduate track and the Top Excellence Award.
Resources
The repository contains training and inference code, experiment notes, presentation slides and qualitative comparisons. Model weights are not currently included in the public release.

projects.title: LG Aimers: Pitch Control Prediction
projects.summary: Predicting and calibrating pitch-control success probabilities from game context and historical player data.
sections: Problem
Estimate pitch-control success before a pitch using the count, runners, player characteristics and historical observations. The test season differs from the seasons used for training.
Approach

Led feature development, model comparison, validation and submission. Combined tree-based models and residual signals with segment-wise probability calibration, using chronological validation to study season changes.
Result
Finished 88th on the hackathon leaderboard with a score of 1,149.33143. Completed the LG Aimers 9th program.
Resources
The public repository documents the selected submission and its feature, model and inference structure. See its README for the released files and execution requirements.

projects.title: Next-Action Prediction for Coding Agents
projects.alt: Distribution of the 14 tool-action classes in the training data
projects.summary: Predicting a coding agent’s next tool action with session-level validation, controlled input experiments and compact inference.
sections: Problem
Predict the next tool action among 14 classes from conversation history and agent state, while meeting submission size and execution-time constraints.
Approach

Led the project and organized parallel analysis and model experiments. Split validation by session to avoid mixing records from the same conversation across training and evaluation. Packaged the ensemble with vocabulary reduction and int8 conversion.
Controlled comparison

Compared input designs on the same 14,001-example validation set. The baseline reached Macro-F1 0.7562, added cues 0.7542, and reordered input 0.7565, indicating that the tested input changes had little effect.
Resources
The repository includes source code, analysis figures, experiment records and the documented inference package.

projects.title: Text-Guided Image Colorization
projects.summary: Colorizing grayscale images from text with DDColor and FLUX candidates, selected per image using CLIP similarity.
projects.result: Undergraduate Excellence Award, BK21 Director’s Award
sections: Problem
Recover color from a grayscale image while following the objects and colors described in a text prompt.
Approach

Led the project from model selection and evaluation to final submission. Generated candidates with DDColor and FLUX.1-dev with ControlNet, then used CLIP ViT-L/14 to select the candidate that best matched each text description.
Result
Received the undergraduate Excellence Award (BK21 Director’s Award) in the 2025 Text-Guided Colorization AI Challenge at Inha University.
Resources
The repository includes integrated inference code, model-specific notebooks and submission packaging. See the README for required model access and input data.

projects.title: Uniroad
projects.alt: Public Uniroad admissions counseling service interface
projects.summary: An admissions counseling service that connects structured admissions data and student context to answers with source citations.
sections: Context

University admissions decisions depend on institution-specific documents and a student’s individual record. The service retrieves relevant source material rather than relying only on a language model’s stored knowledge.
Work

As a co-founding member and AI researcher from March to July 2026, designed the admissions data structure and Agentic RAG engine. Developed contextual answers from uploaded student records and a workflow that cites original sources and abstains on low-confidence questions.
Product operations
Built automated community answers and short-form content for organic acquisition. Continued providing external support after July 2026.
Service
Explore the admissions counseling service through the link above.

projects.title: COSFLOW at UPFLOW
projects.alt: UPFLOW public AI workflow automation service presentation
projects.summary: Regulation search and request-form automation for cosmetic OEM teams, using MCP collection and retrieval-grounded reports.
sections: Problem
Cosmetics manufacturing teams repeatedly search regulatory sources across countries and transfer unstructured customer requests into standard forms.
Work

Built MCP-based collection across five countries and a LangChain RAG engine that generates reports with supporting sources. Compared five language models on real work scenarios and used structured outputs to produce standard request forms.
Evaluation
Tested complex ingredient names and negative constraints such as “free from” requirements, then organized recognition errors into improvement tasks. The company progressed to a paid pilot.
Experience
Co-founding member and AI researcher at UPFLOW from February to October 2025.

projects.title: Training-Free Subject-Driven Image Editing
projects.summary: Reimplementation and extension of subject-driven image editing with diffusion models, including partial-region editing.
sections: Research context
Studied subject-driven image editing at the Multimodal AI Lab, Inha University, from December 2024 to December 2025.
Work
Reproduced and extended training-free editing methods and explored how conditioning and region selection affect identity preservation and background changes.
Attribution

This is a reproduction and extension project. The upstream Diptych Prompting paper belongs to its original authors and is not listed as my publication. The repository describes the upstream method and local implementation.
